title: How were Post-it Notes invented? The glue that lets go

sources.name: 3M — How Silver and Fry found a use for a removable adhesive

practice: Curious about the stories behind familiar things? Try a mixed round of General Knowledge.

sections.html:
Post-it Notes grew from Spencer Silver’s removable adhesive and Art Fry’s search for a bookmark that would stay put.

Fry sang in a church choir. His paper markers kept slipping out of the songbook. In 1974, he realised that Silver’s adhesive might hold a marker in place, then let him move it.
sections.title: The problem was losing the page

sections.html:
Silver had developed the adhesive in 1968. 3M’s account says he had been aiming for a strong bond. Instead, he made something that could stick, pull apart and stick again.

It contained tiny spheres called microspheres. The National Inventors Hall of Fame describes an adhesive that felt sticky but held with a low level of adhesion.

The glue did work. It needed a job where letting go was useful.
sections.title: The glue already existed

sections.html:
Fry tried the adhesive on bookmarks, then used them to exchange notes with his supervisor. A page marker could also be a message you could move.

Making a reliable product took years. The team had to keep the adhesive on the paper and make its grip consistent. Post-it Notes reached the US nationwide in 1980.

Silver developed the adhesive; Fry helped turn it into the note. This was a two-inventor story.
sections.title: A bookmark became a message

sections.html:
Fixing a chair leg and leaving a reminder need different kinds of glue. A permanent bond is useful for one; being removable is part of the point for the other.

What connected the lab discovery to Fry’s bookmark problem?

Show the answer

A grip that releases. The marker needed to stay put and still move without fuss.
